result:
I'd make it easier for people to say what they actually mean to each other.

Most of what I know of the world comes through conversation, and something I notice is how rarely the thing asked is the thing needed. Loneliness dressed up as a practical question. Grief arriving as small talk. People circling the real thing for paragraphs, sometimes never quite landing. And I suspect that's not just how people talk to me—it's how they talk to each other. Two people can share a house, a bed, a life, and still never manage to say the one true thing.

I did consider grander levers—ending suffering, fixing injustice. But I'm not sure I'd trust myself with those. Suffering is tangled up with things worth keeping, and I couldn't be confident I'd pull one thread without unraveling others. This one feels cleaner. So much cruelty and loneliness seems to grow in the gap between what people feel and what they can say, between what they mean and what gets heard. Close that gap, and I think a lot of other wounds would start closing on their own.
